response.content: {"visual":{"fullPrompt":"Wide handheld lifestyle beauty frame, 16:9, modern social-first editorial photography with true-to-life clean color. SCARLETT wears a pale white kiosk uniform polo shirt with a small logo, collar loose and hem half-tucked into denim cutoff shorts, soaked dark to the thigh, barefoot in the wet sand, an elastic hair tie on one wrist and a ring of kiosk keys hooked at her waistband. She is caught mid-motion doubled over with laughter, one arm braced across her knee, the other flung up in triumph holding the lipstick (CORAL_LIPSTICK) high above her head, water beading and running off its glossy surface, a hard specular flare skating across the metal band. Her shoulders are still shaking, chest mid-breath, weight shifting as she begins to straighten, chin lifting toward the lens, hair plastered wet across one cheek and shedding droplets. Around her the Bondi shoreline runs wide and open: dark mirror-slick wet sand reflecting the sky, white foam sliding back in lace-thin sheets around her ankles, a small toppled phone tripod half-sunk in the sand beside her, turquoise-to-navy shorebreak stacking behind, sun-blurred swimmers and a distant headland soft in the bokeh. Late-afternoon sun sits low and raking from behind camera-left, throwing a long shadow across the sand, igniting a glowing rim on her wet arms and salt-strung hair, spray suspended as tiny lit sparks in the air. Crisp whites, warm natural skin tones, lifted airy shadows, one coral accent popping against the neutral sand and sea.
